title: Knowledge Check 3 - Lessons 11-15
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 11-15 - Data 360 Setup and Administration. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A consultant must protect every field that holds a Social Security Number, including fields added next year, without editing permissions each time. What is the right approach?
options: Tag the SSN fields and write a policy keyed on that tag
Set each field's permissions manually every quarter
Hide the entire object in the data model
Rely on the data space prefix to block access
questions.explanation: Tagging the fields and keying a policy on the tag means new fields tagged the same way are protected automatically. Hiding the whole object is the strongest distractor and is wrong because it is far broader than the requirement and blocks legitimate access to non-sensitive fields.

questions.question: An admin tries to delete a tag and the platform blocks it. What is the most likely reason?
options: The tag has too many child tags
The tag is used in a policy
The tag API name is auto-filled
The tag is object level rather than field level
questions.explanation: Tags in use by a policy cannot be deleted until they are removed from the policy. Having many children is the strongest distractor and is wrong because tag hierarchy depth does not block deletion.

questions.question: Which statement about tag hierarchy in Data 360 is correct?
options: Tags support unlimited nesting
A tag can have one parent and multiple children, limited to one level
A tag can have multiple parents
Tags cannot have children at all
questions.explanation: A tag may have a single parent and multiple children, and the hierarchy stops at one level. Unlimited nesting is the strongest distractor and is wrong because the platform enforces a single level of depth.

questions.question: Two policies apply to the same field: one allows a group to read it, another denies the same group. What is the result?
options: Allow wins because it is more specific
Deny wins and access is blocked
The two policies cancel out
The most recently created policy wins
questions.explanation: The rule of precedence is that a deny policy always overrides an allow policy, so access is blocked. The recency distractor is wrong because creation order does not matter; deny is always authoritative.

questions.question: A consultant needs service agents to see only the last four digits of a Social Security Number while finance sees the full value. Which governance feature fits?
options: Tag propagation
Object-level security
Dynamic data masking
A data space prefix
questions.explanation: Dynamic data masking obscures sensitive values at query time and evaluates per user, so agents see redacted data while finance sees the full value. Object-level security is the strongest distractor and is wrong because it controls reach to the whole object, not partial visibility of one field.

questions.question: A team masks a field that another team uses as a join key in record-level security with joins. What happens?
options: The data graph refreshes faster
The tag is automatically deleted
Nothing, joins ignore masked values
The join query returns no results because the key values are masked
questions.explanation: Masking alters the key at query time, so the join finds no matches and record-level security with joins on masked keys returns nothing. The assumption that joins ignore masking is the strongest distractor and is wrong because joins evaluate the masked value.

questions.question: A team needs to promote new identity resolution and calculated insight configuration from a sandbox to production using change sets. Which data kit type must they use?
options: Standard data kit
DevOps data kit
Unlocked package
Local data kit
questions.explanation: Change sets require a DevOps data kit, which is built for sandbox to production promotion. The standard data kit is the strongest distractor and is wrong because standard kits are not supported in change set deployments.

questions.question: Which statement about data kits is correct?
options: A package can hold only one data kit
Data kits carry the records as well as the configuration
Data 360 metadata must be added to a data kit before it can be packaged
A single package must contain both Data 360 and non Data 360 metadata
questions.explanation: Data 360 metadata cannot be packaged directly: it goes into a data kit, and the data kit goes into a package. The claim that kits carry records is the strongest distractor and is wrong because kits carry definitions, not data.

questions.question: An admin deploys a DevOps data kit but it fails with an environment parity error. What is the most likely cause?
options: The kit has too few components
The user was assigned Data Cloud User instead of Data Cloud Architect
The data kit was never published
The target data space name does not match the data space used when the kit was created
questions.explanation: DevOps kits must deploy to the same data space they were created in, and a data space name mismatch triggers an environment parity failure. The unpublished-kit distractor is wrong because an unpublished kit would not reach the deploy stage at all.

questions.question: An admin created a Data 360 sandbox and the connections show Inactive with no data flowing. What is the correct next step?
options: Refresh the sandbox repeatedly
Activate each connection and provide its authorization details
Reinstall the data kit package
Change the data space prefix
questions.explanation: Connections replicate without their stored credentials, so they arrive Inactive and must be activated with fresh authorization. Refreshing the sandbox is the strongest distractor and is wrong because a refresh does not carry credentials into the sandbox either.

questions.question: Which step must happen before the Data Cloud Setup menu becomes available in a new Data 360 sandbox?
options: Publishing a data kit
Matching production licenses so the Data Cloud license syncs
Enabling the left side navigation
Creating a custom permission set
questions.explanation: The sandbox inherits Data Cloud licenses from production, so Match Production Licenses must complete before the Data Cloud Setup menu is available. Publishing a data kit is wrong because it comes after the sandbox is provisioned and configured, not before.

questions.question: A team deploys a DevOps data kit with the Connect REST API and the request times out. What is the most likely fix?
options: Add more components to the kit
Deploy to a different data space
Set async mode so the deployment processes asynchronously
Remove the Data Cloud Architect permission set from the user
questions.explanation: The Connect REST API deploy is asynchronous, and omitting async mode can make the request time out before completion. Removing the permission set is the strongest distractor and is wrong because Data Cloud Architect is required for the deploy, not a cause of the timeout.

questions.question: A CRM data stream fails with an INVALID_FIELD error. What should the admin check first?
options: The data space prefix
Whether the field still exists and the connector permission set still has View All Fields on the object
The SFTP file size
Whether async mode is set
questions.explanation: INVALID_FIELD means a field was deleted or access to it was lost, so confirm the field exists and the connector still has Read, View All Records, and View All Fields. The SFTP file size distractor is wrong because that would produce a STREAM_JOB_STATUS_FAILURE error, not INVALID_FIELD.

questions.question: An SFTP data stream fails with STREAM_JOB_STATUS_CANCELLED. What is the most likely cause?
options: Two consecutive jobs ran on the same data stream
A governance tag was applied to a field
The data kit was never published
The CRM object was deleted in the connected org
questions.explanation: STREAM_JOB_STATUS_CANCELLED occurs when two consecutive jobs run for the same data stream, so only one job should run at a time. The deleted-CRM-object distractor is wrong because that produces an INVALID_TYPE error on a CRM stream, not a cancellation on SFTP.

questions.question: Rows are being rejected during ingestion and the team wants to inspect the offending records. Where do they look?
options: The Setup Audit Trail
The Problem Records DLO via Data Explorer
The Feature Manager
The data space permission set
questions.explanation: Problem records that fail ingestion are isolated into a Problem Records DLO, which you inspect in Data Explorer to find the root cause. The Setup Audit Trail distractor is wrong because it records configuration changes, not rejected data rows.
